items.q: Which enzyme catalyzes the committed rate-limiting step of de novo purine nucleotide biosynthesis, converting PRPP to 5-phosphoribosylamine?
items.exp: Glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase transfers an amino group from glutamine to PRPP, forming 5-phosphoribosylamine. It is feedback inhibited by AMP, GMP, and IMP, and stimulated by PRPP.
r: Correct. Glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase catalyzes the committed step of purine synthesis.
Incorrect. PRPP synthetase activates ribose-5-P but PRPP is also used for pyrimidines and salvage.
Incorrect. IMPDH is the committed step for GMP specifically.
Incorrect. Adenylosuccinate synthetase leads to AMP.
items.kp: Glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase catalyzes the committed rate-limiting reaction of de novo purine synthesis, feedback inhibited by AMP, GMP, and IMP.

items.q: In de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis, which cytosolic enzyme catalyzes the rate-limiting formation of carbamoyl phosphate using glutamine, CO2, and two ATP molecules?
items.exp: Cytosolic CPS-II synthesizes carbamoyl phosphate for pyrimidine synthesis using glutamine as nitrogen donor, inhibited by UTP and activated by PRPP. Mitochondrial CPS-I uses ammonium for the urea cycle.
r: Correct. CPS-II is the cytosolic rate-limiting enzyme of pyrimidine synthesis.
Incorrect. CPS-I is mitochondrial and participates in the urea cycle.
Incorrect. Aspartate transcarbamoylase condenses carbamoyl phosphate with aspartate.
Incorrect. Dihydroorotase closes the pyrimidine ring.
items.kp: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II (CPS-II) is cytosolic, uses glutamine, and catalyzes the rate-limiting step of de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis.

items.q: A 14-month-old boy is brought to the clinic for developmental delay, spastic cerebral palsy, dystonic posturing, and orange sandy crystals in his diapers. The mother notes he compulsively bites his lips and fingertips. Which enzyme is deficient?
items.exp: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is an X-linked recessive disorder caused by complete HGPRT deficiency. Purine salvage fails, causing PRPP accumulation, massive purine de novo synthesis, extreme hyperuricemia, gout, choreoathetosis, and compulsive self-mutilation.
r: Correct. Complete HGPRT deficiency causes Lesch-Nyhan syndrome with self-mutilation and hyperuricemia.
Incorrect. APRT deficiency causes 2,8-dihydroxyadenine radiolucent kidney stones without self-mutilation.
Incorrect. ADA deficiency causes severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID).
Incorrect. Xanthine oxidase deficiency causes xanthinuria with low uric acid.
items.kp: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is an X-linked recessive deficiency of HGPRT, characterized by choreoathetosis, cognitive impairment, compulsive self-mutilation, and severe hyperuricemia.

items.q: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency causes severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID). What is the cellular toxic mechanism that depletes both T and B lymphocytes?
o: Accumulation of dATP allosterically inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, blocking DNA synthesis in dividing lymphoblasts
Depletion of ATP halts T-cell receptor transcription
Accumulation of uric acid crystals inside thymic parenchyma
Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase in bone marrow
items.exp: In ADA deficiency, adenosine and deoxyadenosine accumulate; cellular kinases phosphorylate deoxyadenosine to dATP. Excess dATP allosterically binds the activity site of ribonucleotide reductase, shutting off deoxynucleotide production and killing dividing lymphocytes.
r: Correct. dATP accumulation allosterically inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, crippling DNA synthesis.
Incorrect. ATP is not depleted.
Incorrect. Uric acid is actually decreased in ADA deficiency.
Incorrect. Methotrexate inhibits DHFR, not ADA.
items.kp: Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency elevates deoxyadenosine and dATP, which allosterically inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, starving lymphocytes of dNTPs and causing SCID.

items.q: A 9-month-old infant presents with megaloblastic anemia refractory to vitamin B12 and folate, failure to thrive, and developmental delay. Urinalysis shows massive excretion of orotic acid crystals. Blood ammonia is normal. Which condition is present?
o: Hereditary orotic aciduria (deficiency of UMP synthase)
items.exp: Hereditary orotic aciduria is an autosomal recessive deficiency of UMP synthase (bifunctional orotate phosphoribosyltransferase and OMP decarboxylase). Blood ammonia is normal (unlike OTC deficiency where hyperammonemia is prominent). Treatment is oral uridine.
r: Correct. UMP synthase deficiency causes hereditary orotic aciduria with megaloblastic anemia and normal ammonia.
Incorrect. OTC deficiency causes marked hyperammonemia and respiratory alkalosis.
Incorrect. CPS-I deficiency causes hyperammonemia with low orotic acid.
Incorrect. Lesch-Nyhan causes hyperuricemia, not orotic aciduria.
items.kp: Hereditary orotic aciduria (UMP synthase deficiency) presents with megaloblastic anemia and urinary orotic acid with normal ammonia, treated with oral uridine.

items.q: Allopurinol is metabolized by xanthine oxidase into oxypurinol (alloxanthine), which acts as which type of inhibitor against xanthine oxidase?
o: Suicide (mechanism-based) irreversible inhibitor that remains tightly bound to the molybdenum active site
Reversible competitive inhibitor easily displaced by xanthine
items.exp: Allopurinol is oxidized by xanthine oxidase to oxypurinol, which coordinates tightly to the reduced molybdenum(IV) center of the enzyme as a mechanism-based suicide inhibitor, inactivating it for hours.
r: Correct. Oxypurinol coordinates tightly to the active-site molybdenum as a mechanism-based inhibitor.
Incorrect. It acts as a suicide/tight-binding inhibitor, not a simple easily displaced competitive drug.
Incorrect. It does not activate salvage directly.
Incorrect. It does not bind PRPP synthetase.
items.kp: Allopurinol is converted by xanthine oxidase into oxypurinol, which acts as a mechanism-based inhibitor binding the active-site molybdenum to suppress uric acid synthesis.

items.q: Which enzyme converts ribonucleotides (NDPs) into deoxyribonucleotides (dNDPs) required for DNA replication, and is inhibited by hydroxyurea in sickle cell disease?
items.exp: Ribonucleotide reductase reduces all four ribonucleoside diphosphates (ADP, GDP, CDP, UDP) to their corresponding deoxy forms (dNDPs). Hydroxyurea scavenges the tyrosyl free radical in the active site, inhibiting the enzyme.
r: Correct. Ribonucleotide reductase converts ribonucleotides to deoxyribonucleotides and is inhibited by hydroxyurea.
Incorrect. Thymidylate synthase converts dUMP to dTMP, inhibited by 5-FU.
Incorrect. DHFR reduces DHF to THF, inhibited by methotrexate.
Incorrect. DNA polymerase replicates DNA.
items.kp: Ribonucleotide reductase reduces ribonucleoside diphosphates to deoxyribonucleoside diphosphates; it is inhibited by hydroxyurea and allosterically regulated by dATP.

items.q: 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is a widely used antineoplastic antimetabolite. Its intracellular metabolite 5-FdUMP potently inhibits which enzyme to block thymidine synthesis?
items.exp: 5-FdUMP covalently binds thymidylate synthase and N5,N10-methylene-THF, forming a suicide ternary inhibitory complex that permanently halts conversion of dUMP to dTMP, starving tumor cells of thymidine.
r: Correct. 5-FdUMP forms an irreversible suicide complex with thymidylate synthase.
Incorrect. Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.
Incorrect. Hydroxyurea inhibits ribonucleotide reductase.
Incorrect. 6-mercaptopurine inhibits PRPP amidotransferase.
items.kp: 5-Fluorouracil (via 5-FdUMP) acts as a suicide inhibitor of thymidylate synthase, depleting dTMP required for DNA synthesis.

items.q: Methotrexate and trimethoprim inhibit which enzyme required to regenerate tetrahydrofolate (THF) from dihydrofolate (DHF)?
items.exp: Dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) reduces DHF back to active THF. Methotrexate (human) and trimethoprim (bacterial) competitively inhibit DHFR, depleting the THF pool needed for purine and thymidylate synthesis.
r: Correct. Methotrexate and trimethoprim inhibit dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR).
Incorrect. Thymidylate synthase generates DHF from methylene-THF.
Incorrect. Serine hydroxymethyltransferase transfers hydroxymethyl groups.
Incorrect. Methionine synthase requires B12.

items.q: Which immunosuppressive antimetabolite is metabolized to 6-thiosine monophosphate (6-TIMP) by HGPRT, inhibiting glutamine-PRPP amidotransferase and de novo purine synthesis in lymphocytes?
items.exp: Azathioprine is converted to 6-mercaptopurine, which is activated by HGPRT to 6-TIMP. 6-TIMP inhibits PRPP amidotransferase and IMP dehydrogenase, suppressing purine synthesis in rapidly dividing lymphocytes.
r: Correct. 6-MP and azathioprine are salvaged by HGPRT to active purine synthesis inhibitors.
Incorrect. Mycophenolate mofetil inhibits IMP dehydrogenase directly.
Incorrect. Cyclophosphamide is an alkylating agent.
Incorrect. Tacrolimus is a calcineurin inhibitor.
